text:
Some say we should remove from the poem

personal regrets,

remain abstract, there is some reason for this, but

God!

Twelve lost poems and I have no copies!

And you took my paintings too, the best ones!

It’s intolerable!

Are you trying to fuck me over like the others?

Why didn’t you take my money instead? Usually

they take it from the sick sleeping and drunken pants in the

corner.

Next time take my left arm or a

fifty-dollar bill,

but not my poems.


I’m not Shakespeare

but maybe one day I won’t write anymore,

abstract or otherwise;

There will always be money and whores and drunks

until the last bomb falls,

but as God said,

with his legs crossed:

“it seems I have created many poets

but not so much poetry.”

translation.title: To the Bitch Who Took My Poems
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version of Charles Bukowski. The profanity, direct address, quoted final lines, and stanza breaks are retained.
